title: Indonesia confirms 24 killed in candy factory fire as search continues
html:
Authorities in Indonesia have confirmed the deaths of 24 people in a fire that gutted a candy factory over the weekend, as rescuers continue to search for about 30 missing people.

Said Iqbal, a presidential adviser on labour issues, told reporters on Monday that preliminary reports indicated the blaze may have been caused by a short circuit in an air-conditioner.

He said he would be summoning the factory’s chief executive.

The fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Cikande, Serang regency, West Java province.

The search continued on Monday, with remaining hotspots and the building’s increasingly unstable structure posing safety risks ⁠for rescuers, said Al Amrad, head ⁠of the Banten province search and rescue agency.

He told reporters that 29 people were confirmed safe, five of whom were treated in hospital. Rescuers had so far taken away 24 body bags.

Steven Erwin Wijaya, the CEO of the factory’s parent company, PT United Family Food, said at an earlier news conference that about 300 people were present at the factory complex for Saturday’s shift.

At a news conference on Sunday, Wahyu Hidayati Dwi Palupi, a police disaster victim identification official, said the intensity of the fire had made it impossible to identify the recovered victims visually. She said they would collect DNA samples from relatives and the personal belongings of the missing workers, a process that could take two to three weeks.

Photos and videos circulating online on Sunday showed flames and thick smoke coming from the factory, which borders the capital, Jakarta. Footage from inside the three-storey building appeared to show the fire had caused extensive damage, with equipment blackened and destroyed.

Indonesia has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.

A fire in an office building in Jakarta killed at least 22 people in December last year.

An explosion at an Indonesian nickel-processing plant on Sulawesi island killed at least 13 people in 2023.
summary: Rescuers search for 30 people still missing.
